messages.speaker: user
messages.text: I chair a consortium of eight university labs that wants a shared computational workspace for notebooks, data dictionaries, and reproducible environments. Every lab currently maintains its own mix of servers and personal drives. A two-semester grant can fund migration and training, and the deans want a September launch. The difficulty is that several units support pieces of the service without seeing the whole workspace as theirs.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Separate the launch project from the authorities and work that continue after migration. Map hosting, identity, backup, scientific decisions, data classification, environment maintenance, user intake, and support. For each item, capture the time horizon and the unit that has actually accepted it rather than relying on a general statement of institutional support.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Central IT will provide virtual machines, institutional login, nightly backup, and restoration under its standard infrastructure agreement. The library offers data-management consultations but does not administer software. The research office owns controlled-data policy and incident escalation. Each lab owns the scientific validity of its notebooks and decides who joins its projects.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Put those commitments in an authority table with explicit exclusions. Central IT can own infrastructure health without becoming the application help desk. The library can advise on data plans without approving access. The research office can set controlled-data rules without maintaining environments. Lab responsibility for science and membership should remain visible beside those shared functions.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: The grant pays two platform engineers, a half-time project manager, and four graduate migration assistants from August through June. It also covers training materials and office hours. The grant terms prohibit salaries or cloud charges after June 30. Central IT's hosting contribution continues under its existing agreement, but the temporary platform positions end with the grant.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Mark every launch assignment with the June 30 boundary. The migration plan can be complete for its funded period while later service expectations require their own recorded commitments. Track which tasks end, which transfer under an existing agreement, and which have only a proposal date.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: The steering draft approves a September service for two semesters. The project team will migrate five pilot labs, run weekly intake, maintain the base images, answer user questions, and triage access requests through June. Central IT remains responsible for machines, login, backup, and restoration. The draft does not amend any unit's standing charter beyond those commitments.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: For the launch document, tie each weekly activity to the temporary team and list the interfaces with Central IT, the library, research office, and labs. Include response times and escalation paths for the two-semester period. Keep charter changes and later appropriations as separate decisions requiring their own authority.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: We have three data tiers. Open and ordinary institutional data can use the standard workspace. Controlled human-subject data needs research-office approval, named project members, encrypted storage, and a logged export. Export-controlled or clinical data remains on specialist systems unless the relevant office signs an exception. Labs cannot move a project between tiers on their own.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Turn the tiers into admission checks. The project manager can verify the approval and member list, Central IT can enforce the storage controls, and the research office can decide exceptions. Record rejected or redirected projects as such instead of creating an informal technical workaround.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Some labs use old geospatial libraries and custom compilers. The platform engineers can test the top twenty environments before launch. If an environment fails, they can pin a working image, export the notebook and data dictionary, or leave that project on its existing server. One lab insists that migration is all-or-nothing because partial support will confuse students.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Use a project-level compatibility decision rather than a universal migration promise. Publish the supported image list and test record. A lab can keep an incompatible project on its current server while other projects move. The export package and named image give students a visible boundary between supported and local environments.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: For controlled projects, the research office wants any unexplained access event to pause that project immediately. Central IT would preserve logs and restore from the last clean backup. The principal investigator and research office would decide whether access resumes. Other projects should continue unless the same infrastructure is implicated.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Write the pause at project scope, with authority to widen it when the evidence identifies shared infrastructure. Record who preserves logs, who restores data, who evaluates the research conditions, and who signs resumption. Test the notification chain and one restoration before admitting controlled projects.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: The pilot labs logged the questions they currently handle informally. Across a year they expect about forty new project intakes, monthly environment updates for twelve common images, roughly sixty access changes, data-tier consultations, failed-job triage, and recurring requests to reproduce old analyses for publications or audits. The demand does not end when migration ends.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Quantify that workload by task, frequency, skill, and service expectation. Ask each unit to mark which work falls under an existing commitment, which it could accept with resources, and which it declines. Keep the estimates separate from the launch staffing schedule so the steering council can see both time horizons.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: The responses came back. Central IT will not answer notebook, package, or failed-job questions. The library can offer four consultations a month but cannot run intake or environment maintenance. The research office will handle policy questions and incidents, not ordinary access triage. The labs rejected a rotating duty because six lack the relevant engineering staff. The estimate for the remaining work is about one full-time specialist plus part-time coordination, and no unit accepted that assignment.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Record the responses beside the workload estimate and existing agreements. For the council packet, show the activities, the temporary coverage through June, the portions already accepted by named units, and the alternatives that would require money or a charter change. Do not replace a declined assignment with an assumed handoff.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Three options are being discussed for the following year: member-lab fees for a central specialist, a recurring dean's-office line, or a funded rotation among the two labs with platform staff. None has approval. The budget office will accept a proposal for its February cycle, and the steering council can recommend an option, but it cannot appropriate funds or change a unit charter.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Prepare the three options with cost, service level, collection method, employment home, and the authority needed to adopt each. The February date is useful for a decision packet, but the packet should distinguish a recommendation, an appropriation, and a unit's acceptance of responsibility.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: The launch acceptance test now covers institutional login, tier enforcement, one controlled-project pause, restoration from backup, image versioning, notebook export, and the support escalation directory. A failed restoration blocks launch. A failed optional image blocks only that project and invokes the export or existing-server path.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Run the acceptance test with representatives from Central IT, the research office, a pilot lab, and the temporary platform team. Preserve the test result and exception owner. The launch meeting can approve the service only when the required controls pass and every accepted exception has a dated response.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: One neuroscience lab found that its image breaks after the operating-system patch. The engineers reproduced the failure, pinned the previous image, exported the notebook, and left the lab's active analysis on its existing server. The September migration list now excludes that project while the other four labs remain on schedule.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Add the pinned image, export hash, existing-server location, and affected project to the exception record. The lab can retest after the next image release. Keep the remaining launch acceptance results separate so one compatibility exception does not obscure the status of login, backup, tier controls, or other projects.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: The council signed the two-semester launch memorandum. It incorporates the authority table and acceptance test, keeps Central IT's existing infrastructure agreement unchanged, and ends the temporary project positions June 30. The budget office acknowledged a February proposal slot but made no commitment for the following year.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: File the signed memorandum, existing agreements, acceptance results, exception record, workload estimate, unit responses, and February proposal requirements as separate records. The project manager can report against the launch memorandum while the council prepares any later request under the budget process.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: I will proceed with the September launch and chair the February proposal work. The project manager accepted delivery and support coordination through June. Today I cannot assign a unit to the later service or spend beyond the grant, so the options paper will identify the authority and funding action required for each model.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: The kickoff packet now contains the launch team's signed responsibilities, test evidence, exception path, and June boundary. The options paper records the February submission date, named preparers, and separate signature lines for council recommendation, budget approval, and unit acceptance.
